title: Reconstruct BERT
summary: Rebuild bidirectional pretraining from input representation through normalization and GELU-based encoder blocks.

parts.title: Bidirectional context
parts.prompt: How does masked language modeling let BERT use both left and right context without copying the target token?
parts.answer: Selected tokens are hidden or corrupted before encoding, so the representation can attend in both directions while the original token remains unavailable at its own input position.
hints: The corruption prevents a trivial identity solution.

parts.title: Segment-aware inputs
parts.prompt: What information is added by token, position, and segment embeddings?
parts.answer: Token embeddings identify lexical items, position embeddings encode order, and segment embeddings distinguish sentence A from sentence B. Their sum forms each encoder input.
hints: Self-attention alone has no inherent token order.
Sentence-pair tasks need a source indicator.

parts.title: Pretrain then fine-tune
parts.prompt: Why can one pretrained encoder support classification, tagging, and question answering with small task heads?
parts.answer: The shared objectives learn contextual representations useful across tasks. Fine-tuning adapts all parameters while a small head converts the relevant token representations into task-specific outputs.
hints: Which representation is commonly used for classification?
Token-level tasks retain every contextual vector.

parts.title: Implement LayerNorm
parts.prompt: Normalize across the final feature dimension and apply gamma and beta.

parts.title: Implement GELU
parts.prompt: Implement the tanh approximation to GELU used in Transformer feed-forward blocks.
